// Generated by the RipulAgent package's RipulThemeRedirect build-tool plug-in.
// It is written into the build folder on every build and is not part of your sources.
//
// Inside this module the declarations below are chosen over SwiftUI's of the same name,
// so `.font(.body)`, `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and `Color(.systemBackground)` in
// your own files follow the theme with no line of them changed. With no theme each one
// returns exactly what SwiftUI's would have (docs/theming-for-hosts.md).
//
// To leave a part out, add its flag to the target's Swift compilation conditions:
//   RIPUL_THEME_NO_ROOT     keep SwiftUI's WindowGroup; put `.ripulThemeRoot()` on your root yourself
//   RIPUL_THEME_NO_STYLES   keep SwiftUI's foregroundStyle; the hierarchy styles stay the system's
//   RIPUL_THEME_NO_LISTS    keep SwiftUI's List, Form and Section; lists stay the system's
//   RIPUL_THEME_NO_TEXT     keep SwiftUI's Text initialisers; text with no colour stays the system's

import SwiftUI
import RipulThemeKit
#if canImport(UIKit)
import UIKit
#endif

// MARK: Text styles and system fonts

extension Font {
    static var largeTitle: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.largeTitle) }
    static var title: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.title) }
    static var title2: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.title2) }
    static var title3: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.title3) }
    static var headline: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.headline) }
    static var subheadline: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.subheadline) }
    static var body: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.body) }
    static var callout: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.callout) }
    static var footnote: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.footnote) }
    static var caption: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.caption) }
    static var caption2: Font { RipulThemeRedirect.font(.caption2) }

    static func system(size: CGFloat, weight: Font.Weight? = nil, design: Font.Design? = nil) -> Font {
        RipulThemeRedirect.systemFont(size: size, weight: weight, design: design)
    }

    static func system(_ style: Font.TextStyle, design: Font.Design? = nil, weight: Font.Weight? = nil) -> Font {
        RipulThemeRedirect.systemFont(style, design: design, weight: weight)
    }

    // The font itself. These only let a symbol keep its system size (see `Image.font`).
    func weight(_ weight: Font.Weight) -> Font { RipulThemeRedirect.weight(self, weight) }
    func bold() -> Font { RipulThemeRedirect.bold(self) }
    func italic() -> Font { RipulThemeRedirect.italic(self) }
}

extension Image {
    /// A font on a symbol is its size, not type: it keeps the system's.
    /// (`Font`, where SwiftUI's takes `Font?`: the closer match is the one chosen.)
    func font(_ font: Font) -> some View {
        RipulThemeRedirect.iconFont(self, font)
    }
}

// MARK: Colours

extension Color {
    static var red: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.danger) }
    static var orange: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.warning) }
    static var green: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.success) }
    static var blue: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.info) }
    static var gray: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.neutral) }
    static var primary: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.text) }
    static var secondary: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.textSecondary) }

    /// A colour of your asset catalogue is a role of the asset's name: a theme document
    /// that names it under `roles` changes it, and until one does it is the asset.
    init(_ name: String, bundle: Bundle? = nil) { self = RipulThemeRedirect.color(named: name, bundle: bundle) }

    #if canImport(UIKit)
    init(_ color: UIColor) { self = RipulThemeRedirect.color(color) }
    init(uiColor: UIColor) { self = RipulThemeRedirect.color(uiColor) }
    #endif
}

extension ShapeStyle where Self == Color {
    static var red: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.danger) }
    static var orange: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.warning) }
    static var green: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.success) }
    static var blue: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.info) }
    static var gray: Color { RipulThemeRedirect.color(.neutral) }
}

#if !RIPUL_THEME_NO_STYLES
// `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.tertiary` and `.quaternary`. Not generic, where SwiftUI's
// is: for a hierarchy style this is the closer match, and every other style is SwiftUI's.
extension View {
    func foregroundStyle(_ style: HierarchicalShapeStyle) -> some View {
        RipulThemeRedirect.foregroundStyle(self, style)
    }
}

extension Text {
    func foregroundStyle(_ style: HierarchicalShapeStyle) -> Text {
        RipulThemeRedirect.foregroundStyle(self, style)
    }
}
#endif

// MARK: Text with no colour of its own

#if !RIPUL_THEME_NO_TEXT
/// The lines of this target on which a text has no colour of its own: none in its chain
/// of modifiers, none from a view round it, and not a control's label. Read from the
/// source on every build, so a new text is here without anyone adding it.
private let ripulThemeRedirectBareText: [String: Set<UInt>] = {
    let lines: [String: [UInt]] = [/*BARE-TEXT*/:]
    let module = String(#fileID.prefix { $0 != "/" }) + "/"
    return Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: lines.map { (module + $0.key, Set($0.value)) })
}()

// A text made on one of those lines is given the theme's text colour when a theme names
// one. `#fileID` and `#line` are the call site's. With no theme each is SwiftUI's own text.
extension Text {
    init(_ key: LocalizedStringKey, ripulFile: String = #fileID, ripulLine: UInt = #line) {
        self = RipulThemeRedirect.text(key) { ripulThemeRedirectBareText[ripulFile]?.contains(ripulLine) == true }
    }

    // Disfavoured as SwiftUI's own string form is, so a literal stays a localised key.
    @_disfavoredOverload
    init(_ content: String, ripulFile: String = #fileID, ripulLine: UInt = #line) {
        self = RipulThemeRedirect.text(verbatim: content) { ripulThemeRedirectBareText[ripulFile]?.contains(ripulLine) == true }
    }
}
#endif

// MARK: Lists

#if !RIPUL_THEME_NO_LISTS
/// SwiftUI's `List`, its ground, rows and separators in the theme's surfaces once a theme
/// names them. With no theme it sets the system's own values.
struct List<SelectionValue: Hashable, Content: View>: View {
    private enum Selection {
        case none
        case one(Binding<SelectionValue?>?)
        case many(Binding<Set<SelectionValue>>?)
    }
    private let selection: Selection
    private let content: Content

    init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where SelectionValue == Never {
        selection = .none
        self.content = content()
    }

    init(selection: Binding<SelectionValue?>?, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) {
        self.selection = .one(selection)
        self.content = content()
    }

    init(selection: Binding<Set<SelectionValue>>?, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) {
        self.selection = .many(selection)
        self.content = content()
    }

    init<Data: RandomAccessCollection, RowContent: View>(_ data: Data, @ViewBuilder rowContent: @escaping (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
    where Content == ForEach<Data, Data.Element.ID, RowContent>, Data.Element: Identifiable, SelectionValue == Never {
        selection = .none
        content = ForEach(data, content: rowContent)
    }

    init<Data: RandomAccessCollection, ID: Hashable, RowContent: View>(_ data: Data, id: KeyPath<Data.Element, ID>, @ViewBuilder rowContent: @escaping (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
    where Content == ForEach<Data, ID, RowContent>, SelectionValue == Never {
        selection = .none
        content = ForEach(data, id: id, content: rowContent)
    }

    init<Data: RandomAccessCollection, RowContent: View>(_ data: Data, selection: Binding<SelectionValue?>?, @ViewBuilder rowContent: @escaping (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
    where Content == ForEach<Data, Data.Element.ID, RowContent>, Data.Element: Identifiable {
        self.selection = .one(selection)
        content = ForEach(data, content: rowContent)
    }

    init<Data: RandomAccessCollection, RowContent: View>(_ data: Data, selection: Binding<Set<SelectionValue>>?, @ViewBuilder rowContent: @escaping (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
    where Content == ForEach<Data, Data.Element.ID, RowContent>, Data.Element: Identifiable {
        self.selection = .many(selection)
        content = ForEach(data, content: rowContent)
    }

    var body: some View {
        switch selection {
        case .none: RipulThemeRedirect.list(SwiftUI.List { RipulThemeRedirect.rows(content) })
        case .one(let selected): RipulThemeRedirect.list(SwiftUI.List(selection: selected) { RipulThemeRedirect.rows(content) })
        case .many(let selected): RipulThemeRedirect.list(SwiftUI.List(selection: selected) { RipulThemeRedirect.rows(content) })
        }
    }
}

/// SwiftUI's `Form`, themed as a list is.
struct Form<Content: View>: View {
    private let content: Content

    init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) { self.content = content() }

    var body: some View { RipulThemeRedirect.list(SwiftUI.Form { RipulThemeRedirect.rows(content) }) }
}

/// SwiftUI's `Section`, its header and footer in the theme's family and secondary colour.
struct Section<Parent: View, Content: View, Footer: View>: View {
    private let parent: Parent?
    private let content: Content
    private let footer: Footer?

    init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content, @ViewBuilder header: () -> Parent, @ViewBuilder footer: () -> Footer) {
        parent = header(); self.content = content(); self.footer = footer()
    }

    init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content, @ViewBuilder header: () -> Parent) where Footer == EmptyView {
        parent = header(); self.content = content(); footer = nil
    }

    init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content, @ViewBuilder footer: () -> Footer) where Parent == EmptyView {
        parent = nil; self.content = content(); self.footer = footer()
    }

    init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where Parent == EmptyView, Footer == EmptyView {
        parent = nil; self.content = content(); footer = nil
    }

    init(_ title: LocalizedStringKey, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where Parent == Text, Footer == EmptyView {
        parent = Text(title); self.content = content(); footer = nil
    }

    init<S: StringProtocol>(_ title: S, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where Parent == Text, Footer == EmptyView {
        parent = Text(title); self.content = content(); footer = nil
    }

    var body: some View {
        if let parent, let footer {
            SwiftUI.Section { content } header: { RipulThemeRedirect.sectionHeader(parent) } footer: { RipulThemeRedirect.sectionFooter(footer) }
        } else if let parent {
            SwiftUI.Section { content } header: { RipulThemeRedirect.sectionHeader(parent) }
        } else if let footer {
            SwiftUI.Section { content } footer: { RipulThemeRedirect.sectionFooter(footer) }
        } else {
            SwiftUI.Section { content }
        }
    }
}
#endif

// MARK: The root

#if !RIPUL_THEME_NO_ROOT
/// SwiftUI's `WindowGroup`, with the theme root round its content. The theme is the one
/// Info.plist names under `RipulTheme`.
private func ripulThemeRedirectRoot<Content: View>(_ content: @escaping () -> Content) -> RipulThemeRedirect.Root<Content> {
    #if DEBUG
    RipulThemeRedirect.useUsageMap(ripulThemeRedirectUsageMap)
    #endif
    return RipulThemeRedirect.Root(content)
}

struct WindowGroup<Content: View>: Scene {
    private let scene: SwiftUI.WindowGroup<RipulThemeRedirect.Root<Content>>

    init(@ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> Content) {
        scene = SwiftUI.WindowGroup { ripulThemeRedirectRoot(content) }
    }

    init(id: String, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> Content) {
        scene = SwiftUI.WindowGroup(id: id) { ripulThemeRedirectRoot(content) }
    }

    init(_ title: LocalizedStringKey, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> Content) {
        scene = SwiftUI.WindowGroup(title) { ripulThemeRedirectRoot(content) }
    }

    init(_ title: LocalizedStringKey, id: String, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> Content) {
        scene = SwiftUI.WindowGroup(title, id: id) { ripulThemeRedirectRoot(content) }
    }

    var body: some Scene { scene }
}
#endif

// MARK: The View Explorer's map

/// Which theme tokens each identified element of this target is drawn with, read from its
/// source when it was built. A Debug build only: it names files and lines.
private let ripulThemeRedirectUsageMap = #"""
/*USAGE-MAP*/
"""#
#endif
